message.content:
This appears to be a CBP ruling covering a wrist strap and a key chain. Key chains classify in 7117.19 (imitation jewelry) or 7117.90, or in 7113 (precious metal). The wrist strap is a chain with charms, so it may also be imitation jewelry or a similar article.

I recall a ruling on "Live Love Bark Charm Wristlet Strap," which I believe put the wrist strap in 4202.99.9000 as an item carried in the pocket or handbag, or in 7117.19.9000. Key chains with charms are typically classified in 7117.19.9000, imitation jewelry of base metal, other. Key rings proper fall under 7117 only if they are jewelry-like. Heading 7117 covers imitation jewelry, but key chains are often classified under 7117 when they are decorative. Heading 7117 excludes articles of 8306, and key rings are in 8306? Not exactly; split key rings are in 8305 or 7326.

The wrist strap is most likely imitation jewelry in 7117.19, since it is a decorative chain with charms. I would classify both in 7117.19.9000. The 7117.19 subheading is "Imitation jewelry of base metal, other"; its statistical suffixes are 7117.19.9000 for other, and 7117.19.50 for items not plated with precious metal. Cufflinks and studs are 7117.11. The 7117.19.90 line is "Other," and I will go with it. The single answer must cover both items, so I choose 7117.19.9000.
